Activation.description: When a rule runs without being named by its code or name (ADR-018).

oneOf.description:
In the default selection, and matched by a prefix or `ALL`, while the rule is exact;
whatever its certainty with `lint.heuristic`.
Only by its exact code or name.

Selected as an exact `Default` rule is, whatever its certainty: it reports only what a
declared contract asks for, so declaring the contract is what selects it.

Certainty.description:
Whether a report can be wrong about the code (ADR-018). A report's claim is a conjunction of
premises (its rule page lists them under "What a report states").

oneOf.description:
Every premise of the claim was established, under the assumptions R1-R5, and the rule's
reports were checked on the measurement corpus with none wrong: a wrong one is a bug.

A premise of the claim may be unknown, which does not stop the report: it can be wrong
about the code.

Certification.description: The certification of an exact rule (docs/precision.md, "How a rule becomes exact").

census.description: Every report on the development corpus, checked by hand.

holdout.description: Every report of one run on the frozen holdout corpus.

real_bugs.description:
The real bugs it found (docs/precision.md, "Rare failures"), for a rule with fewer than 10
exact reports in its census and holdout run.

rule.description: The code of the certified rule.

Checked.description:
Reports checked by hand, the false claims found among them, and the harm of the right ones
where the run classed it.

false_claims.description: The reports found wrong about the code.

harm.description: The right reports by class; left out when the run did not class them.

Consequence.description: What happens in the code a rule reports, which sets its default severity.

oneOf.description:
A bug that can be critical: a wrong result, an exception, a lost update, a deadlock, an
event loop held up for every other task, or a broken contract.

A bug that is rarely harmful: a promise the code makes is broken, such as a read-only
annotation, where the callers seldom notice.
Slower code that computes the right result.

id.description: `<kind>.<name>`, stable while the feature is experimental (`rule.MUT101`).

reason.description: Why the feature is experimental, as whole sentences.

since.description: The release the feature is experimental in first.

target.description: What the feature is: a rule code, a command, an option, a key, or a behavior.

tracking.description: An issue or discussion that tracks what keeps the feature experimental.

ExperimentalKind.description: How an entry names its target.

oneOf.description: A command (`heki inspect`), its options and output included.
A command and one of its options (`heki check --generate-prompt`).
A key below `[tool.heki]`, with its tables (`lint.relax-async-in-tests`).
An output format and one of its fields (`json fix`).
A behavior no single name selects, described in words.

Harm.description:
The right reports of a run by class (docs/precision.md): confirmed, plausible, and benign, and
those the run left without a class.

benign.description: Reports that are right, of code that is deliberate or harmless at realistic sizes.

confirmed.description: Reports whose problem is real and observable from the code.

plausible.description: Reports that are right, of code that does harm at realistic sizes.

unclassified.description: Right reports the run left without a class.

Premise.description: One premise of an exact claim.

decided_in.description:
Where heki decides it (`crate::module::item`): the one home every rule reading the
premise goes through. Several entries are steps of one decision, in order.

name.description: The name the rule pages give it, unique in the table.

states.description: What it states, as the rule pages state it.

PublishedMeasurement.description:
A measurement as published: the classes of the sampled reports, and the shares derived
from them.

benign.description: Reports that are right, of code that is deliberate or harmless at realistic sizes.

confirmed.description: Reports whose problem is real and observable from the code.

date.description: The date of the build the round measured.

false_claims.description: Reports that are wrong about the code.

plausible.description: Reports that are right, of code that does harm at realistic sizes.

real_harm_percent.description: The share of real harm (confirmed and plausible), in percent.

right_percent.description: The share right about the code (confirmed, plausible, and benign), in percent.

round.description: The round of the measurement protocol.

rule.description: The code of the measured rule.

RuleFamily.description: The family a rule belongs to, which its code starts with.

oneOf.description: Changes of objects other code holds.
Effects: blocking calls and what a function runs.
Slower code that computes the right result.

RuleRecord.description: A rule as `heki rule --output-format json` prints it.

auto_fix_default.description: Whether `--fix` applies the rule's fix by default.

certainty.description: The certainty of the rule's reports at most: heuristic until the rule is certified.

certification.description: How the rule became exact; none for a rule that is not certified.

default_enabled.description: Whether the rule runs with no configuration.

default_severity.description: The severity the rule's reports have unless the configuration overrides it.

doc.description:
Ruff-style documentation (`crates/heki_rules/rule-docs/<CODE>.md`): printed by
`heki rule <CODE>` and published as the rule's page.

experimental.description: Why the rule is experimental; none for a stable rule.

heuristic_note.description:
What a heuristic rule's reports mean and how the rule is selected; none for an exact
rule.

measurement.description: The latest measurement of how often its reports are right about the code.

premises.description:
The premises of the rule's exact claim (`heki_rules::premises`), empty for a rule
without one.

size_dependent_fix.description: A proven-safe rewrite that `--fix` applies only with `--include-size-dependent`.

slug.description: The name of the rule (`async-blocking-call`), which also names its page.

summary.description: One line saying what the rule reports.

unsafe_fix.description:
A fix that may change what the program does: `--fix` and `--diff` apply it only with
`--unsafe-fixes`, and the language server offers it as a quick fix that is not preferred.

description: `heki rule` prints one rule, or an array of every rule.
title: heki rule --output-format json
